name: Pteranodon
sum: Iconic crested, toothless pterosaur of the Western Interior Seaway, known from about 1,200 specimens.
holotype: YPM 1117 skull (P. longiceps) — Smoky Hill Chalk, Niobrara Formation, Kansas.
material: About 1,200 specimens, many with nearly complete skulls and articulated skeletons.
exceptional: Fish bones in the stomach region and a fish bolus; clear sexual dimorphism in crest and pelvis.
biology: Albatross-like soaring wings; fed on fish, probably dipping or plunge-diving from the surface. Males with huge crests may have competed for harems at offshore rookeries.
